questions.q: Trace the development of the Mughal school of painting under Akbar, Jahangir and Shah Jahan.
answer: The Mughal school of miniature painting was a court art that blended Persian, Indian and later European styles, and it developed distinctively under three great emperors.

answer.text: Though begun under Humayun, who brought Persian masters, the school truly flourished under Akbar. He set up a large imperial atelier where artists like Daswanth and Basawan illustrated great manuscripts such as the Hamzanama, Akbarnama and Razmnama. The style was vigorous, colourful and full of crowded, lively scenes.

Jahangir, a keen connoisseur, encouraged fine naturalism and portraiture. Masters like Ustad Mansur painted birds, animals and flowers with great accuracy, and European influence brought shading and allegory.
Under Shah Jahan painting became more formal, refined and jewel-like, with elegant court scenes and lavish use of gold.

answer: Thus Mughal painting evolved from energetic narrative under Akbar to refined elegance under Shah Jahan.
